title: Classifying special quadrilaterals by their properties
summary: Classify quadrilaterals from sides, angles, diagonals and symmetry.
objectives: Classify special quadrilaterals from their sides, angles and parallel sides.
Use diagonal and symmetry properties to distinguish related quadrilaterals.
Explain the hierarchy linking squares, rectangles, rhombi and parallelograms.

blocks.text: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus. Rectangles and rhombi are parallelograms. A kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides, while a trapezium has one pair of parallel sides in this course classification.

Quadrilaterals form a hierarchy. Every square is also a rectangle, rhombus and parallelogram. Every rectangle and every rhombus is a parallelogram. A kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides, while a trapezium has one pair of parallel sides under the syllabus convention used here.

Classify a figure by the most specific set of guaranteed properties. Sides and angles often narrow the class first; diagonals then distinguish related shapes. Rectangle diagonals are equal and bisect each other. Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other. Square diagonals have both sets of properties.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: A parallelogram has equal diagonals. Classify it.

sections.verification_note: The result follows the stated property and satisfies the original geometric conditions.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: A parallelogram has perpendicular diagonals and one right angle. Classify it as specifically as possible.

content.text: One right angle in a parallelogram makes all four angles right angles, so it is a rectangle.
Perpendicular diagonals in a parallelogram also make it a rhombus.
A quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus is a square.

sections.verification_note: A square satisfies every stated property: opposite sides parallel, four right angles and perpendicular bisecting diagonals.

blocks.text: Do not stop at a broad name when a more specific one is guaranteed. Equal diagonals alone do not prove a square, and perpendicular diagonals alone do not prove a square. Combine all given properties before classifying.

prompt.text: How many lines of symmetry does a non-square rectangle have?

feedback.text: Its two midlines are symmetry axes; its diagonals are not.
